⭐☆☆☆☆ (1/5)

BeamNG.drive is one of the most frustrating games I've ever played. The driving physics are realistic, but they're so unforgiving that even the smallest mistake can completely destroy your vehicle and force you to restart. It feels more like you're being punished than having fun.

The AI traffic is inconsistent and often behaves unpredictably, leading to crashes that don't feel like your fault. Many maps feel empty, with very little to do beyond driving around or crashing. The career mode still feels incomplete, and a lot of the gameplay revolves around making your own fun instead of having structured content.

Performance is another major issue. Even on decent hardware, the game can struggle with frame rates, especially when using AI traffic or multiple vehicles. Loading times can also be long.

The controls take a long time to get used to, and the game doesn't do a great job of introducing new players to its mechanics. If you're expecting an accessible driving game or a racing experience, you'll probably end up disappointed.

Overall, BeamNG.drive has impressive technology behind it, but the actual gameplay feels repetitive, unfinished, and difficult to enjoy. I can't recommend it in its current state.

citations.review_text:
Just bought this game, and I'm so glad I did! Less than 20 minutes into playing, I paused the game just to write this review.

I've had this game on my wishlist for years, and now I finally understand why people say there's nothing else like it. I also play games like Forza, but [b] this game brings out the child in me! [/b]

The realistic soft-body damage models, convincing physics, and incredible collision mechanics make every crash feel amazingly authentic. The attention to detail is outstanding.

This game is amazing. Just buy it! I only wish I'd picked it up years ago. You won't regret your purchase.

Hats off to the developers—five stars!

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Experienced sandbox drivers point to heavy CPU requirements balanced by convenient mod management and detailed independent part deformation.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires a capable computer and is heavy on system resources, particularly the CPU.

citations.review_text: A great bit of fun. BeamNG.drive is an overly-complicated softbody physics simulation, in the best way possible. It makes for dramatic crashes, driving with consequences and realism not achieved in any other driving game, despite its graphical flaws (which have recently been addressed and are much better!). It's a great game, but be warned, it is CPU intensive and hard to run.

I've had this game since 2020 and I still haven't gotten bored of it. Important thing to understand first: this isn't a racing game. It's a physics and crash simulator above everything else.

The physics carry the whole game:
Every vehicle is built from a frame and individual components calculated in real time (soft-body physics). Damage isn't a canned animation — the metal actually bends and crumples based on the angle and speed of the impact. Hit the same pole twice and you'll get two different results. I haven't seen another game come close to this level of detail.

Content:

Large, varied open maps — deserts, cities, mountains, twisty canyon roads — each one detailed enough to make you want to explore it
A wide range of vehicles, and you can modify every part: chassis, engine, suspension, tires. Drop in an engine from a completely different car and see how it behaves
Scenarios, challenges, and a career mode if you want structure — plus a pure sandbox if you just want to experiment and break things
The modding scene is enormous and the repository is built into the game, so you install mods with one click and effectively never run out of content

Why I'd recommend it:
The value for the price is excellent, and it's been getting consistent updates for years — you buy it once and it keeps growing. Even if you only launch it to wreck cars, you'll look up and realize you've put dozens of hours in without noticing.

Be realistic about:

It leans heavily on your CPU (especially single-core performance), so weaker systems will struggle, particularly with several vehicles spawned at once
No real licensed cars — everything is an original model inspired by real vehicles
There's a small learning curve with the settings and the driving model. Give it a chance before judging it

Bottom line: If you enjoy physics, experimentation, and controlled chaos, buy it without hesitation. If you want a competitive racing game in the vein of Forza or Gran Turismo, this…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the soft-body physics system, noting that vehicle parts, frames, and components deform and react independently during crashes.

citations.review_text:
There are racing games, there are driving simulators, and then there's BeamNG.drive.

Calling this game a "car crash simulator" is selling it incredibly short. The crashes are impressive, but they're only the result of what makes BeamNG so special: one of the most sophisticated soft-body physics systems ever created in a consumer game.

Unlike traditional racing games, where a vehicle is essentially a rigid object with a damage texture slapped on after an impact, every vehicle in BeamNG is built from a network of interconnected nodes and beams. Every suspension arm, chassis rail, driveshaft, and body panel reacts to forces independently. Hit a curb too hard and your steering geometry changes. Clip a guardrail and your wheel alignment is ruined. Land a jump poorly and your suspension compresses unevenly, permanently affecting how the car drives.

Nothing feels scripted.

Every crash is unique because the physics determine the outcome in real time. The angle of impact, speed, weight distribution, suspension setup, and momentum all influence what happens next. Two crashes at nearly identical speeds can produce completely different results.

The attention to detail goes far beyond destruction.

Weight transfer feels natural while cornering. Body roll changes depending on the vehicle. Tires lose grip progressively rather than instantly. Different drivetrains behave differently under acceleration. Off-roading feels genuinely mechanical instead of arcade-like, and every vehicle has its own personality because its engineering is actually modeled rather than approximated.

What amazes me most is how educational BeamNG can be.

You don't just see why a vehicle loses control—you understand it. You can feel oversteer develop because too much weight shifts rearward. You can watch suspension components fail under excessive load. You begin appreciating concepts like momentum, center of gravity, chassis rigidity, and suspension geometry simply by driving.

Then there's the variety.…

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the soft-body physics engine as a standout feature that enables realistic vehicle crashes and damage simulation.

citations.review_text:
# BeamNG.drive Review ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (10/10)

BeamNG.drive is hands down one of the best driving simulators ever made. The soft-body physics are unmatched, making every crash, jump, and collision feel incredibly realistic. No two accidents are ever the same, and the vehicle damage system is still the best in the genre.

What makes BeamNG stand out is its freedom. Whether you want to drift, race, off-road, crawl over rocks, haul cargo, roleplay, or just launch cars off giant ramps, the game lets you do it all. The maps are large and detailed, the vehicle customization is extensive, and the built-in mod repository adds thousands of high-quality cars, maps, and scenarios to keep the game fresh.

The game continues to receive regular updates that improve vehicles, maps, gameplay, and overall performance, showing just how dedicated the developers are to making BeamNG.drive even better.

The only downside is that BeamNG can be demanding on your PC, especially if you're running multiple AI vehicles. However, if your system can handle it, the experience is absolutely worth it.

**Pros:**

* Incredible soft-body physics
* Realistic driving and crash simulation
* Huge variety of vehicles and maps
* Endless replayability with mods
* Regular updates and improvements

**Cons:**

* Requires a fairly powerful PC for the best experience
* Career mode is still being expanded

**Final Rating: 10/10**

If you're a car enthusiast, drifter, simulator fan, or just someone who enjoys experimenting with realistic vehicle physics, BeamNG.drive is an easy recommendation. It's not just a game—it's the ultimate driving sandbox.
